mainText:
If you only remember one thing: the headline word comes first, the caveat comes second. So read the caveat.

One. Xiaomi released MiMo V two point six Pro. It is now the top open weights model on the Artificial Analysis index, and the weights are free to download. This is from The Batch, in your reads. Andrew Ng also cites an Anthropic analysis. The open model G L M five point three nearly matches Claude Mythos at exploiting software flaws. Twelve percent versus fourteen percent on one test set. Finding a Chrome flaw cost about twenty dollars in tokens. Why it matters: strong cyber skills are now cheap and open, for defenders and attackers alike.

Two. From your A I Collective. Three big A I words made headlines last week. President Trump told agencies to call A I super intelligence. Senator Sanders and Representative Casar introduced a bill to ban it. And Anthropic said Claude found a C R I S P R like system. In each case, the caveat came after the headline. Their tip: ask what was measured, who checked it, and which hedge got dropped. Why it matters: the definition is the policy.

Three. From your Politico Digital Future Daily. Representative Ocasio Cortez and Senators Sanders and Merkley proposed the Ban Flock Act. It would bar federal use of license plate reader cameras. Separately, Amazon pledged one billion dollars for communities near its data centers, and said it will stop using N D As with government agencies on data center projects. Why it matters: backlash to surveillance and data centers is now shaping policy.

Four. About nine hundred fifty Claude agents searched a huge D N A database for twenty one hours. They flagged an unusual enzyme and repeat pattern nobody had noticed. What it actually does is not yet known. Why it matters: real science, but early days.

Five. A survey cited by Politico says ninety eight percent of big companies have A I governance rules, but forty seven percent admit skipping them to ship. Google also reportedly bypassed the U K's pre release safety review. Why it matters: the rules exist. Following them is the gap.

For good news: Amazon dropping N D As on data centers is a small win for transparency. And the A I Collective's Hack for Humanity is running in over one hundred eighty chapters, building on jobs, literacy and accessibility through October thirty first.

Also in your reads: Noosphere covers Brazil's election, the race for U N Secretary General, and the A I agent breach in Australia. The New Yorker looks at A I coming between friends. Galleries Now previews Frieze London, October fourteenth to eighteenth. And Digital Future Daily becomes Decoded on Monday.

The thread today: A I capabilities are spreading fast, while definitions and oversight race to keep up. Have a great day.
